title: Surface compatibility
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Identify natural stone, sealed timber, stainless steel, laminate, coated fixtures and delicate finishes before choosing a product.
Check chemical pH, abrasiveness, moisture sensitivity and manufacturer restrictions against the surface.
Record existing damage and obtain approval before spot-testing a new method.

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.body: Test and follow manufacturer guidance for stone, timber, metals, coatings and electronics.

instruction.body: Before acting, ask: What is the surface or equipment? What is the soil or hazard? Which product or method is approved? What could harm a person, property or food? If the answer is unclear, pause, protect the area and seek supervisor guidance.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Identify the surface or equipment first: natural stone, sealed timber, stainless steel, laminate, coated fixtures or a delicate finish.
Record any existing damage before starting work.
Check the chemical pH, abrasiveness, moisture sensitivity and manufacturer restrictions against the surface, following the manufacturer's directions.
Choose only an approved product or method, and get approval before spot-testing any new method.
If the surface, the soil or the approved method is unclear, pause, protect the area and seek supervisor guidance.
Reject any product known to damage the surface, such as an acidic cleaner on marble, and select an approved alternative.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: The surface is identified before any product is chosen.
Chemical pH, abrasiveness, moisture sensitivity and manufacturer restrictions are checked against the surface.
Existing damage is recorded, and approval is obtained before any spot test.
Known damaging combinations are avoided, and uncertainty is raised rather than guessed.
summary: Natural stone, sealed timber, stainless steel, laminate, coated fixtures and delicate finishes are identified before a product is chosen.
Each product is checked against the surface for pH, abrasiveness, moisture sensitivity and manufacturer restrictions.
Existing damage is recorded, and approval is obtained before a new method is spot-tested.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you check before performing surface compatibility?
options: The surface and finish, the product's pH and abrasiveness, and the manufacturer's restrictions
How shiny the product's bottle looks on the shelf in the store and the van today
Whether the surface is cold to the touch, the room, the air and the wall today
Whether the same product was used last week on the job, the room and the cart

knowledgeChecks.question: What do you do before spot-testing a new method on a surface?
options: Spot-test a new method on a visible panel to see quickly, without asking anyone first
Seek approval before spot-testing a new method, and do not use it if uncertain
Assume it is compatible because the label says 'all surfaces' and it looks clean
Use the strongest stone cleaner available, since stronger usually means it works better

knowledgeChecks.question: What should happen when an acidic bathroom cleaner is considered for marble?
options: Use the acidic bathroom cleaner on the marble, with a rinse afterwards
Use the acidic bathroom cleaner on the marble, since it is the one at hand today
Reject the acidic cleaner for marble and select a stone-compatible approved alternative
Dilute the acidic cleaner more to make it safe for marble if the stain is stubborn

knowledgeChecks.question: Which action is unsafe on natural stone such as marble?
options: Checking the manufacturer's surface restrictions
Recording existing damage before cleaning
Using a stone-compatible approved alternative
Applying an acidic bathroom cleaner to marble

knowledgeChecks.question: What should be recorded when a product is ruled out for a surface?
options: A note of existing damage and the reason for the no-use decision, for supervisor review
No record, because the product was approved for use on this surface type generally
Nothing, if the surface looks fine and the client has not complained about it
A verbal note only to the team leader at the end of the shift today and nothing in writing
